acceptance: The CLI and the Python API apply one scale rule for `tpcds_obt`, recorded with its reason on this item.
`num_queries` for `tpcds_obt` is 90, after every consumer of the field was checked (CLI listing, MCP, doc-contracts and docs-data exports, test matrices, UAT).
TPC-DS OBT runs end to end on DuckDB at SF 0.01, 0.1 and 1, and at SF 10 if claimed.
A regression test shows the CLI accepts each enabled scale and rejects one outside the rule.
A changelog fragment records the change.
The report gives the accepted rule, per-scale row count, Parquet size and generation time with hardware, the PR number, and the core commit whose site-inputs bundle carries the change.
context:
Decision (2026-11-10): tpcds_obt uses the TPC-DS scale rule. `validate_scale_factor` routes `tpcds_obt` to `validate_tpcds_scale`, and `TPCDSOBTBenchmark.__init__` calls the same function, so the CLI and the Python API accept exactly what TPC-DS accepts: 0.001 <= SF <= 100000, with SF >= 1 a whole number (the shared BaseBenchmark rule). Reason: OBT is built from dsdgen output generated by `TPCDSDataGenerator`, which already enforces this range, and `TPCDSOBTTransformer` was written for sub-1 scales (its coverage check is enforced only at SF >= 1). Sub-1 scales are allowed because the project already depends on them: `make tpcds-obt-equivalence` and the nightly `sql-execution-gate-obt` run OBT at SF 0.01. The old `min_scale: 1.0` / `scale_options: [1.0]` came from the bulk metadata shrink in #590 with no recorded OBT reason. `scale_options` (the advertised list used by the CLI preview, interactive selection, MCP discovery and the UAT ladder) lists only scales verified end to end on DuckDB; `min_scale` is removed, matching `tpcds`. `num_queries` becomes 90 (SQL catalog count, matching the TPC-DS convention of counting query numbers, not lettered statements); `query_description` now says 90 SQL queries (93 statements) and 17 DataFrame queries. UAT consequence: the release-gate ladder now enumerates OBT at 0.01/0.1/1.0 on platforms with no OBT runtime envelope (stage 1 eligible pairs 109 -> 117, floor 87 -> 93; stage 3 floor 105 -> 107). The SF1 runtime envelopes for tpcds_obt still prune every scale on spark, clickhouse-server, starrocks, pg-duckdb, pg-mooncake, postgresql, timescaledb, singlestore and questdb (tpcds_obt stays in `_SF1_ONLY_BENCHMARKS`); narrowing them to SF1 would add 12 untested release cells and is left as an owner decision.

Evidence (2026-11-11, Apple M4 10-core, 16 GB RAM, macOS, DuckDB 1.5.5, `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpcds_obt --phases generate,load,power --force datagen`; generation = dsdgen + OBT transform as printed by the CLI): SF0.01 50,335 rows, 14,547,061 B Parquet, gen 9.00 s; SF0.1 503,753 rows, 117,310,038 B, gen 36.34 s; SF1 5,041,336 rows, 1,382,457,481 B, gen 220.29 s; SF10 50,399,818 rows, 18,211,529,635 B, gen 2205.86 s, load 1253.37 s. All 715 columns; every run passed 93 statements x 3 iterations with validation passed. SF1 and SF10 needed BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB=11 (owner-approved): the first SF1 attempt was stopped by the host watchdog at 8.09 GiB footprint against the default 8 GiB. SF0.001: dsdgen hangs on this host for plain TPC-DS too (TPCDSDataGenerator, parallel 1 and 10, no progress in 120 s); pre-existing TPC-DS generator issue, not claimed. SF >= 10000: dsqgen times out on Q9 parameters (30 s) for both TPC-DS and OBT; not claimed. Commit 92b9a23a40 on fix/tpcds-obt-scale-factors.
description:
`benchbox run --benchmark tpcds_obt` rejects every scale factor except 1.0 ("tpcds_obt accepts scale_factor in [1.0]; got 10.0"), and the Python API rejects every scale below 1.0. The restriction looks accidental: the `tpcds_obt` registry block (`default_scale: 1.0`, `scale_options: [1.0]`, `min_scale: 1.0`, `num_queries: 17`) came in with 9f51cc65ee (#590, a bulk metadata shrink with no recorded OBT decision). `validate_scale_factor` special-cases only `tpcds`; `tpcds_obt` is checked against `scale_options`. The project already runs OBT at SF 0.01 through paths that skip the check (`make tpcds-obt-equivalence`, nightly `sql-execution-gate-obt`). `num_queries: 17` is the DataFrame count; the SQL catalog has 90 queries (93 statements, Q14/Q23/Q24 lettered).

The fix lands in core. The site page `BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site: docs/benchmarks/tpc-ds-obt.md` ("Scale Factors" table) is corrected separately once the site-inputs bundle carries the change.
